family: Monitor Deloitte Growth & Innovation / Operating Model

modules.name: Market Entry
modules.framework: Monitor Deloitte market-entry / McKinsey Three Horizons

findings.Red: Entry is a hope. TAM, ICP, and competitive map are not gated.
findings.Yellow: A thesis exists; kill-criteria and capital envelope do not.
findings.Green: Entry has a thesis, owner, and gates before spend scales.

findings.Red: A second site will invent a second company.
findings.Yellow: Some standards can travel; leadership and estimating cannot yet.
findings.Green: The operating kit is cloneable: CRM, cadence, delivery promise.

modules.name: New Revenue Stream Design
modules.framework: McKinsey core vs adjacency (Zook/Bain core is cousin) — Horizon 2 offer

findings.Red: New offer logic is 'more things for more people.'
findings.Yellow: Adjacency is named but not piloted with kill-criteria.
findings.Green: Same customer new offer, or new customer same capability — not both at once.

findings.Red: The core offer is stagnating and the new bet is undefined.
findings.Yellow: Offers proliferate without a portfolio thesis.
findings.Green: Core, adjacent, and option bets are separate with owners.

modules.name: Operational Scaling
modules.framework: Deloitte operating model 2.0 — scale without a second bottleneck

findings.Red: The core cannot absorb more volume, let alone a new site or stream.
findings.Yellow: Scale is possible if the constraint is named and subordinated.
findings.Green: Throughput can fund a gated expansion.

findings.Red: No P&L leader, no seats, no decision rights for the new bet.
findings.Yellow: Roles are sketched; they collide with the core team.
findings.Green: Horizon-2 has a named leader who does not steal core oxygen.

modules.name: Capital Allocation
modules.framework: Deloitte Enterprise Value Map / Bain ring-fenced growth capital

findings.Red: Expansion spend is hiding inside the core P&L.
findings.Yellow: A budget exists; monthly burn and stage gates do not.
findings.Green: Expansion is a separate envelope with a kill switch.

modules.name: Innovation Readiness
modules.framework: Monitor Deloitte sense-and-respond / Three Horizons governance

findings.Red: The culture treats every new idea as a rescue of the core.
findings.Yellow: Pilots happen; they rarely die or scale on evidence.
findings.Green: Options are funded small, reviewed hard, scaled or killed.

archetypes.name: Expansion Not Ready
archetypes.headline: Do not open the next office or stream until the core can fund it.
archetypes.situation: Market-entry, operating kit, and capital gates are missing while ambition is high.
archetypes.implication: A new site or offer will export today's bottleneck and burn cash.
archetypes.recommendation: Install a business-case gate, ring-fence capital, and clone the operating kit before launch.
rootCause: Horizon-2 is being used to escape a weak Horizon-1
No named P&L leader or kill-criteria
Operating standards will not survive a second site
Capital is not ring-fenced from the core

archetypes.name: Conditional Expansion
archetypes.headline: Expansion is viable as a gated pilot — not as a second company.
archetypes.situation: A thesis exists. Org, capital, and operating clone are incomplete.
archetypes.implication: If you scale spend now, you will staff a hope.
archetypes.recommendation: Time-box a Horizon-2 pilot. Same customer or same capability — not both.
rootCause: Ambition is real; the operating kit is not fully portable
Pilot design is weaker than the narrative
Core constraint still competes with the new bet
Decision rights for kill/scale are fuzzy

archetypes.name: Expansion Ready
archetypes.headline: The core can fund a disciplined Horizon-2. Treat it as a managed option.
archetypes.situation: Entry thesis, kit, and capital envelope are strong enough to launch gated.
archetypes.implication: The risk is unfocused adjacency, not unreadiness.
archetypes.recommendation: Launch with a named leader, shared services, and a 18-month cash curve.
rootCause: Core is healthy enough to export a standard
Adjacency logic can be made explicit
Governance can kill or scale on evidence

initiatives.name: New Office Business Case Gate
initiatives.summary: No geography until TAM, ICP, leader, and 18-month cash curve are explicit.

initiatives.name: New Office Operating Kit
initiatives.summary: Clone estimating, CRM, cadence, and delivery standards before site two invents a new firm.

initiatives.name: Named P&L Leader for New Geography
initiatives.summary: A new office without a single accountable leader becomes a cost center with a sales story.

initiatives.name: New Revenue Stream Thesis
initiatives.summary: Same customer new offer, or new customer same capability — never both at once.

initiatives.name: Horizon-2 Pilot with Kill Criteria
initiatives.summary: Time-boxed pilot with revenue, margin, and capacity gates.

initiatives.name: Ring-Fence Expansion Capital
initiatives.summary: Protect core cash. Expansion spend is a separate envelope with a monthly burn review.

initiatives.name: Shared Services for Multi-Site
initiatives.summary: Finance, estimating, and CRM stay central until volume is proven.

initiatives.name: Market Entry and Competitive Map
initiatives.summary: Where you will win, where you will not, and who already owns the relationships.

initiatives.name: Adjacent Offer Cross-Sell Play
initiatives.summary: Launch the new stream through existing accounts before hunting new logos.

initiatives.name: Offer Portfolio Thesis
initiatives.summary: Core, adjacent, and option offers — three lists, three owners, one capital envelope.

initiatives.name: Name the Scale Constraint First
initiatives.summary: If the core bottleneck is estimating or delivery, a new office exports the same wait.

initiatives.name: Horizon-2 Governance Cadence
initiatives.summary: Monthly option review: evidence, burn, kill/scale. Do not bury it in the core ops meeting.

initiatives.name: Critical Seats for the New Bet
initiatives.summary: Name the seats the strategy requires. Vacancy is a strategic risk.

initiatives.name: 18-Month Expansion Cash Curve
initiatives.summary: Bookings, burn, and breakeven on one page. No curve, no launch.

initiatives.name: Design Partner / First-Five Customers
initiatives.summary: Five named design partners before a brochure. Evidence over theater.
